1.title: Pull the caps off the wires
1.say: Hold the gray box steady with one hand. Twist the small orange caps off the wall wires. Leave the four bare copper ends sticking out of the box.
placements: small orange twist cap on the white wall wire → off the wire and set aside (in the video: upper left of the gray box)
small orange twist cap on the lower wall wires → off the wires and set aside (in the video: middle right of the gray box)
four bare copper wire ends → sticking out of the gray box opening (in the video: two white and two black wires out front)
watch_for: if a bare end slips back inside the box, pull it gently forward again so you can see it
if a cap will not turn, try turning the other way and pull steady
1.check_yourself: It should look like four bare copper ends sticking out of the gray box with no caps on.
1.safety: Switch the breaker off before touching any wire.

2.title: Check the wires have no power
2.say: Touch the red and black probes of the yellow tester to the bare wire ends. Check the tester stays dark and quiet for every pair.
placements: red probe of the yellow tester → to a bare wall wire end inside the gray box (in the video: touching the lower copper twist)
black probe of the yellow tester → to another bare wall wire end at the same time (in the video: touching a second bare end in the box)
watch_for: if you test only one pair, another wire could still be live so test every pair
if the tester lights or beeps, stop and keep the breaker off
2.check_yourself: It should look like the yellow tester touching the bare wires with no light and no sound.
2.safety: Hold only the plastic handles of the probes.

3.title: Join the white wires together
3.say: Hold the two white wall wires side by side. Screw the yellow twist cap onto their bare ends. Push the capped white wires to the back of the box.
placements: two white wall wires → side by side with bare ends even and twisted together (in the video: left and right white wires from the gray box)
yellow twist cap → screwed over both white bare ends (in the video: yellow cap inside the box)
capped white wires → pushed to the back bottom of the gray box leaving two black wall wires out front (in the video: white wires hidden behind)
watch_for: if copper shows below the yellow cap, unscrew it and push the wires deeper
if you leave a white wire out, the heater will not work so use both whites
3.check_yourself: It should look like no white wires showing with a yellow cap tucked inside and two black wires out.
3.safety: Keep the breaker off so the black wires cannot shock you.

4.title: Join thermostat to first black wire
4.say: Hold one short black wire from the thermostat next to the first black wall wire. Screw the red twist cap over both bare ends.
placements: one short black wire hanging from the black thermostat base → alongside the bare end of the first black wall wire from the gray box (in the video: left side of the box opening)
red twist cap → screwed over both bare ends to join them (in the video: large red cap centered in the box opening)
watch_for: if copper shows below the red cap, the joint is shallow so reseat it deeper
if the joint pulls loose, twist the red cap tighter until it holds
4.check_yourself: It should look like one black wall wire joined under a red cap to the hanging thermostat with one black wall wire still free.
4.safety: Keep the breaker off while joining the wires.

5.title: Join thermostat to second black wire
5.say: Hold the remaining thermostat black wire next to the remaining wall black wire. Screw the second red twist cap over both bare ends.
placements: remaining short black wire hanging from the black thermostat base → alongside the bare end of the remaining black wall wire from the gray box (in the video: twisted together above and to the right of the box)
second twist cap → screwed over both bare ends of that pair (in the video: twisted copper joint hanging to the right of the box)
watch_for: if you mix a black wire with a white wire, stop and use only black to black
if copper shows outside the cap, unscrew and push the wires deeper
5.check_yourself: It should look like both black wall wires joined to the hanging thermostat with red caps on.
5.safety: Keep the breaker off while joining the second pair.

6.title: Screw the thermostat flat to box
6.say: Push all the capped wires gently inside the gray box. Hold the black thermostat base flat over the box opening. Drive the top and bottom small silver screws into the box.
placements: black thermostat base with white round knob → flat over the gray box opening centered on the wall (in the video: covering the rectangular hole)
small silver screw at the top of the base → into the top screw hole of the gray box using the driver (in the video: top center of the base)
small silver screw at the bottom of the base → into the bottom screw hole of the gray box using the driver (in the video: bottom center of the base)
watch_for: if wires hold the base off the wall, push the caps deeper inside first
if the base sits crooked, loosen the screws and straighten it before tightening
6.check_yourself: It should look like the black base with the white knob screwed flat over the wall opening.

7.title: Push the white cover on
7.say: Hold the white square cover with the dial facing out. Push it straight over the black base until it clicks.
placements: white square cover with round dial → straight over the black thermostat base centered on the wall (in the video: centered on the white wall over the base)
watch_for: if the cover will not click, it is upside down so turn it around
if a gap shows at the edge, push evenly on all sides until flat
7.check_yourself: It should look like a white square cover with a round dial centered on the wall.
